evidence: "I feel like M is nearby," Jack whispered.
"I'm going to bring the medallion back soon," Jack said loudly. "And the bookmark, too. Both of them. Tomorrow!"
questions.rationale: Jack senses M is near, so he speaks loudly on purpose so that M might hear his promise.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses a theme of this final chapter?

options.A: Solving one mystery can leave an even bigger mystery to explore.
options.B: Friends should always keep their adventures a secret.
options.C: It is safer to stay home than to explore new places.
options.D: Hard work is always rewarded with a good lunch.

evidence: This absolutely proved the tree house belonged to M. There was no doubt about it.
Will we ever meet M? Jack wondered.
questions.rationale: The clue answers who owns the tree house, yet the unanswered question of who M is keeps the larger mystery open.

questions.stem: What two objects does Jack take out of his drawer to bring to the tree house?

options.A: His raincoat and rain boots
options.B: The gold medallion and the leather bookmark
options.C: His notebook and a flashlight
options.D: A castle book and a dinosaur book

evidence: Jack reached into his drawer. He took out the medallion.
Then he took out the bookmark. It was made of blue leather.
questions.rationale: Jack goes to his drawer and takes out the gold medallion and then the blue leather bookmark to carry to the tree house.

questions.stem: How does the green parrot named Polly cause the children's adventure to begin?

options.A: It flies into the tree house and knocks the open book onto the floor
options.B: It appears right after Annie wishes to be in the picture, and then the tree house starts to spin
options.C: It carries the medallion away, so they chase it into the woods
options.D: It reads the title of the book out loud to Jack and Annie

evidence: Annie pointed to the picture. "I wish we were there instead of here," she said.
The tree house started to spin. Faster and faster!
questions.rationale: The parrot from the picture shows up just after Annie makes her wish, and moments later the wind rises and the tree house spins, carrying them away.

questions.stem: In the sentence "The letter M was engraved on it," what does the word "engraved" most nearly mean?

options.A: Cut or carved into the surface
options.B: Painted with bright colors
options.C: Wrapped in leather
options.D: Glued on as a sticker

evidence: It was gold. The letter M was engraved on it.
questions.rationale: The M is engraved on the gold medallion, meaning it is cut or carved into the metal, which is why it matches the M on the tree-house floor.

questions.stem: What can the reader infer about the place shown in the open book Annie finds?

options.A: It is a cold, snowy mountain far from the sea
options.B: It is a warm, sunny place by the ocean with a beach, a palm tree, and a ship
options.C: It is the same rainy Frog Creek woods they just left
options.D: It is a busy city full of tall buildings

evidence: He saw a sunny beach. A big green parrot sitting in a palm tree. And a ship sailing on a blue sea.
Annie pointed to the picture. "I wish we were there instead of here," she said.
questions.rationale: The picture shows a sunny beach, a palm tree, and a ship on a blue sea, so the reader can tell it is a warm place by the ocean—very different from the cold rain outside.

questions.stem: Which sentence best summarizes what happens in this chapter?

options.A: Jack and Annie go to the tree house in the rain, find an open book with a sunny sea, and the tree house spins them away
options.B: Jack and Annie decide it is too wet and stay home instead of visiting the tree house
options.C: Jack and Annie return the castle book and dinosaur book to the M person
options.D: Jack and Annie teach the green parrot Polly how to talk

evidence: But we have to go to the tree house," said Annie.
The tree house started to spin. Faster and faster!
questions.rationale: The chapter follows the two hurrying through the storm to the tree house, discovering the open book that shows a sunny sea, and being whisked away as the tree house spins.

questions.stem: What does Jack notice about the sailing ship's flag when the ship comes closer?

options.A: It is bright green with a palm tree on it
options.B: It is black with a skull and crossbones
options.C: It is white with a large letter M
options.D: It is red and yellow like a rainbow

evidence: The flag was black. With a skull and crossbones.
questions.rationale: As the ship nears, Jack can see its flag, which is black with a skull and crossbones—the sign of pirates.

questions.stem: How do Jack and Annie act differently once the tree house lands by the sea?

options.A: Both of them refuse to leave the tree house at all
options.B: Annie wants to run into the water right away, while Jack wants to study the book first
options.C: Jack jumps in first, and Annie stays behind to read
options.D: Both of them decide to swim out to the sailing ship

evidence: "Come on, let's follow her! Let's go in the water!" said Annie.
“Wait, we have to study the book first,” said Jack.
questions.rationale: Annie is eager to jump straight into the water, but careful Jack wants to study the book before doing anything, showing how their reactions differ.

questions.stem: In the sentence "He shielded his eyes against the sun," what does "shielded" most nearly mean?

options.A: Covered or protected
options.B: Rubbed and scratched
options.C: Closed and rested
options.D: Washed with water

evidence: He shielded his eyes against the sun. And peered out at the sea.
questions.rationale: Jack shields his eyes against the bright sun, meaning he covers or protects them with his hand so he can peer out at the sea.

questions.stem: Why does a chill go through Jack when he sees the ship's flag?

options.A: He realizes the ship is sailing away from them
options.B: He realizes the ship belongs to pirates and may be dangerous
options.C: He is cold because his clothes are still wet from the rain
options.D: He is worried the ship will crash into the palm trees

evidence: The flag was black. With a skull and crossbones.
"Pirates of the Caribbean," Jack read aloud.
questions.rationale: The skull-and-crossbones flag and the book's title tell Jack the ship is a pirate ship, so the chill shows he senses danger coming toward them.

questions.stem: What lesson does this chapter most suggest through what happens to Jack and Annie?

options.A: A beautiful, fun place can still hide a real danger you do not notice at first
options.B: It is always better to swim than to read a book
options.C: You should never leave home when it is raining
options.D: Parrots make the best guides on an island

evidence: Actually, the water did look wonderful.
As he stared at the ship's flag, a chill went through him.
questions.rationale: The children enjoy the wonderful warm water, but the approaching pirate flag shows that even a lovely place can hide danger they only spot too late.

questions.stem: According to the caption Jack reads, what did pirates do three hundred years ago?

options.A: They built stone forts along the coast.
options.B: They raided Spanish treasure ships in the Caribbean Sea.
options.C: They mapped every island in the sea.
options.D: They traded gold with the Spanish navy.

evidence: Three hundred years ago, pirates raided Spanish treasure ships in the Caribbean Sea.
questions.rationale: The caption states directly that pirates raided Spanish treasure ships in the Caribbean Sea.

questions.stem: How do Jack and Annie react differently when Annie first sees the pirates?

options.A: Both of them run for the tree house right away.
options.B: Jack hides in the sand while Annie waves at the pirates.
options.C: Annie draws the flag while Jack watches the boat.
options.D: Annie warns Jack and starts running, but Jack keeps drawing instead of looking up.

evidence: "Jack, some pirates are getting into a rowboat," said Annie.
Jack kept drawing.
questions.rationale: Annie notices the danger and calls out, but Jack is so focused on his drawing that he keeps at it instead of reacting.

questions.stem: Jack saw something "glinting in the sand." What does glinting most likely mean here?

options.A: shining with small flashes of light
options.B: sinking down slowly
options.C: making a loud noise
options.D: moving on its own

evidence: Jack saw something glinting in the sand. He reached for it. It was his glasses.
questions.rationale: Because the object turns out to be his glasses catching the light, "glinting" means shining with small flashes of light.

questions.stem: Why does Jack run back toward the water even though the pirates are coming?

options.A: He wants to fight the pirates by himself.
options.B: He is trying to hide the rowboat from Annie.
options.C: He left the pirate book propped in the sand and does not want to lose it.
options.D: He dropped his glasses near the shore.

evidence: Suddenly Jack saw the pirate book. In all the confusion he had forgotten it. It was still propped in the sand.
"I'll be right back!" Jack called. "I've got to get the book!"
questions.rationale: Jack realizes he forgot the pirate book in the sand, so he runs back to grab it before it is lost.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes Chapter 3?

options.A: Jack and Annie sail out to meet the pirate ship and make friends with the crew.
options.B: Jack learns about pirates and draws their flag, then he and Annie must flee as three pirates row ashore and charge at them.
options.C: Annie reads about the Jolly Roger while Jack looks for his lost glasses in the sand.
options.D: Jack and Annie find pirate treasure buried under a palm tree on the beach.

evidence: He started drawing the Jolly Roger flag.
Three big pirates splashed onto the sand.
questions.rationale: The chapter moves from Jack studying pirates and drawing their flag to the children fleeing as three pirates land and rush at them.

questions.stem: What does the biggest pirate call himself?

options.A: Pinky
options.B: Stinky
options.C: Cap'n Bones
options.D: Jolly Roger

evidence: "No one escapes Cap'n Bones!" he roared. His breath was terrible.
questions.rationale: The biggest pirate roars that no one escapes Cap'n Bones, naming himself.

questions.stem: What does Annie do that shows she is brave even after Cap'n Bones grabs Jack?

options.A: She charges up to the biggest pirate, calls him a bully, and hits and kicks him.
options.B: She quietly climbs back up into the tree house.
options.C: She offers the pirates the medallion so they will let Jack go.
options.D: She runs down the beach to get help from Pinky and Stinky.

evidence: "Leave him alone, you bully!" she cried.
She hit the pirate with her fist and kicked him.
questions.rationale: Instead of hiding, Annie confronts the huge pirate, insults him, and physically fights back, showing her courage.

questions.stem: The chapter is titled "Vile Booty," and Cap'n Bones keeps yelling about wanting gold, not books. In pirate talk, what does booty mean?

options.A: a pirate's boots
options.B: an old sailing map
options.C: a kind of sea bird
options.D: stolen treasure or valuable loot

evidence: "Aghh, books," growled Cap'n Bones. He spit on the sand. "I want gold, you dogs!"
"Gold! Gold! Gold!" he cried.
questions.rationale: Cap'n Bones treasures gold and scorns books, so "booty" means the stolen treasure or valuable loot pirates hunt for.

questions.stem: What can the reader infer about why Cap'n Bones suddenly drops Jack and Annie?

options.A: He decides the children are not worth his time.
options.B: He sees the shiny gold medallion and cares far more about the treasure than about them.
options.C: He hears his ship calling him back to sea.
options.D: He is frightened by the gleeful shriek from the tree house.

evidence: Pinky leaned out the tree house window. He held the medallion. It glimmered in the sunlight.
Cap'n Bones dropped Jack and Annie. He caught the medallion as it fell.
questions.rationale: The moment the gold medallion appears, Cap'n Bones lets the children go to grab it, showing greed for treasure outweighs holding them.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses a theme suggested by Chapter 4?

options.A: Greed for gold can control a person, making treasure matter more to them than anything else.
options.B: Reading books is a waste of a pirate's time.
options.C: It is always safer to give bullies whatever they ask for.
options.D: The biggest and strongest person always wins in the end.

evidence: "I hate books! Keep looking, dogs! Find me something good!"
"Gold! Gold! Gold!" he cried. Cap'n Bones threw back his head and laughed horribly.
questions.rationale: Cap'n Bones ignores everything but gold and forgets the children the instant treasure appears, showing how greed can take over a person.

questions.stem: What does Cap'n Bones pull out of his belt pouch to show Jack and Annie?

options.A: A gold coin from the treasure
options.B: A torn treasure map
options.C: A loaded pistol
options.D: A letter from Captain Kidd

evidence: He reached into a belt pouch and pulled out a torn piece of paper. He waved it at Jack and Annie.
"Is that a treasure map?" asked Jack.
questions.rationale: Bones pulls a torn piece of paper from his pouch, and Jack recognizes it as a treasure map.

questions.stem: Why does Cap'n Bones make Jack read the map instead of reading it himself?

options.A: Bones cannot read, so he needs the children to read it for him.
options.B: Bones wants to test whether the children are telling the truth.
options.C: The writing on the map is in a language only Jack knows.
options.D: Bones is too busy aiming his pistols to hold the map.

questions.stem: Why does Grandmother let Black Hawk only show the buffalo, not hunt them?

questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：They have enough meat, and the Lakota never take more buffalo than they need.

questions.stem: How does Annie say they can ride the ponies without saddles or reins?

options.A: Tie ropes around the ponies’ necks to steer them.

and grip with your legs.

questions.stem: Jack lets out a wild whoop after he sees Grandmother watching him. Why?

questions.stem: According to the research book, how many bison were on the Great Plains at the beginning of the 1800s?

options.B: 40 million.
options.C: 2 thousand.
options.D: 6 million.

questions.stem: Looking at the huge herd, Jack “knew for certain” what time they had come to. What did he figure out?

options.A: They had come before the white settlers arrived and before the great herds ended.

options.D: Black Hawk shoots an arrow toward it.

The huge buffalo jerked its head up.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：Black Hawk sneezes loudly right beside it.

questions.stem: Which event happens LAST in this chapter?

options.A: All the buffalo stop running and begin grazing again.

options.D: Black Hawk creeps on all fours toward the buffalo.

options.C: Black Hawk says she has good medicine; Jack says she just has a way with animals.
options.D: Black Hawk says she used a magic spell; Jack says she read it in Morgan’s book.

She just has a way with animals.

questions.stem: “On her face was a look of amazement.” Here “amazement” means ___.

options.A: 愤怒；生气
options.B: 疲倦；劳累
options.C: 伤心；难过
options.D: 惊奇；惊讶

evidence: On her face was a look of amazement.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“惊奇；惊讶”。

questions.stem: What was the beautiful lady who helped Annie wearing?

options.B: A fringed buckskin dress.
options.C: A blue feathered robe.
options.D: A gray wolf-skin cape.

questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：A white leather dress.

questions.stem: When Annie mentions the lady in white, Black Hawk’s “eyes had grown wide.” This suggests that Black Hawk ___.

options.A: thinks Annie is making up a silly story to impress him

options.C: 开心地

“having a long tail.”

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes this chapter?

questions.stem: When the monkeys, peacocks, and deer suddenly start crying out, why does Jack put Teddy in his pack?

questions.stem: What happens when the tiger leaps at Jack and Annie as they swing on the vines?

options.A: He grabs Jack’s backpack and pulls it down to the ground.
options.B: He catches hold of a vine and climbs up after them.
options.C: His claws barely miss them, and he crashes back down into the bushes.
options.D: He knocks Annie off her vine into the tall grass.

evidence: His claws barely missed Jack and Annie!
The tiger crashed back down into the bushes.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：His claws barely miss them, and he crashes back down into the bushes.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes this chapter?

options.A: Jack and Annie swing away from the python, barely escape a leaping tiger, and then discover a herd of elephants below their tree.
options.B: Jack and Annie fight off the python with sticks, chase the tiger away, and climb down to look for the tree house.
options.C: Jack and Annie fall from their vines, hide deep in the bushes, and wait all night for the langurs to return.
options.D: Jack and Annie ride the tiger through the forest, feed the hungry elephants, and find the gift in a tree.

evidence: Like a flame, a tiger leaped up from the bushes!
In the gray gloom, they saw a herd of elephants.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：Jack and Annie swing away from the python, barely escape a leaping tiger, and then discover a herd of elephants below their tree.

questions.stem: Why does Annie think riding on an elephant is a good way to travel through the forest?

options.A: Elephants can run much faster than any tiger in the forest.
options.B: The elephant knows exactly where the forest gift is hidden.
options.C: Riding an elephant is the only way to cross the deep stream.
options.D: Their book said tigers don’t attack elephants, so they would be safe.

evidence: Our book said tigers don’t attack elephants, right?
So we should travel through the forest on the back of an elephant,” said Annie.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：Their book said tigers don’t attack elephants, so they would be safe.

questions.stem: Who leads the way as the elephants march through the forest?

options.A: Teddy, barking from the front.
options.B: Annie, steering Saba by her ears.
options.C: Kah and Ko, the two langurs.
options.D: A group of small deer.

evidence: Kah and Ko bounded ahead of them, two moon shadows leading the way.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：Kah and Ko, the two langurs.

questions.stem: When a long roar split the night, “A chill went down Jack’s spine.” This means Jack ___.

options.A: 觉得夜里太冷，想穿外套
options.B: 突然感到害怕，背脊发凉
options.C: 从大象背上滑下来摔伤了背
options.D: 高兴得浑身发抖

evidence: Suddenly, a long roar split the night.
A chill went down Jack’s spine.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“突然感到害怕，背脊发凉”。

questions.stem: When Annie says the elephant “just told me” her name is Saba, Jack says, “Yeah, right.” This shows that Jack ___.

options.A: doesn’t believe an elephant could really tell Annie her name
options.B: thinks Saba is a beautiful name for an elephant
options.C: already knew the elephant’s name from the book
options.D: is upset that Annie climbed onto the elephant first

evidence: “That’s her name,” said Annie. “She just told me.”
“Yeah, right,” said Jack.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：doesn’t believe an elephant could really tell Annie her name

questions.stem: Which event happens LAST in this chapter?

options.A: Annie climbs down onto Saba’s back first.
options.B: Jack falls asleep with his head on Saba’s back.
options.C: Saba rests her trunk on Jack’s head.
options.D: A long roar splits the night and turns into moaning.

evidence: Soon Jack’s head rested on Saba’s back.
questions.rationale: 按照本章事件先后顺序，最先/最后发生的是：Jack falls asleep with his head on Saba’s back.

questions.stem: Where is Annie when Jack wakes up on Saba’s back?

options.A: Sitting barefoot on a big black rock downstream.
options.B: Riding on the back of another elephant.
options.C: Sleeping inside the magic tree house.
options.D: Swinging on vines with Kah and Ko.

evidence: She was sitting on a big black rock downstream. She was barefoot and soaking wet.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：Sitting barefoot on a big black rock downstream.

questions.stem: The book says the Indian rhino is “a very endangered animal. This means that there are not many left.” “Endangered” means ___.

options.A: 非常危险、会伤人的
options.B: 只生活在水里的
options.C: 视力很差的
options.D: 濒临灭绝的；数量很少的

evidence: The Indian rhino is a very endangered animal. This means that there are not many left.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“濒临灭绝的；数量很少的”。

questions.stem: According to Jack’s book, why do rhinos sometimes charge at things by mistake?

options.A: Because they are always hungry.
options.B: Because loud noises make them angry.
options.C: Because they do not see well.
options.D: Because they are guarding their babies.

evidence: But because they do not see well, they sometimes charge at things by mistake.
Too bad animals can’t wear glasses, he thought.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：Because they do not see well.

questions.stem: How does the information in Jack’s book help Annie when the rhino points his horn at her?

options.A: Jack knows rhinos are afraid of dogs, so Annie calls for Teddy and the rhino runs away.
options.B: Jack knows a loud noise will usually stop a rhino, so Annie claps and shouts and the rhino stops.
options.C: Jack knows rhinos cannot swim well, so Annie wades into deeper water to escape.
options.D: Jack knows rhinos love flowers, so Annie offers the rhino a white flower to eat.

evidence: “Make a loud noise!” Jack yelled.
The rhino stopped. He grunted. Then he sank back into the water.
questions.rationale: 结合人物与事件的关系，正确的是：Jack knows a loud noise will usually stop a rhino, so Annie claps and shouts and the rhino stops.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes this chapter?

options.A: Jack wakes up in the tree house, finds that Annie is gone, and searches the forest for her until the sun goes down.
options.B: Jack wakes up on Saba’s back, rides her across the wide stream, and catches silver fish for everyone’s breakfast.
options.C: Jack wakes up by a misty stream, slides off Saba into the mud, and reads about rhinos just before one rises from the water and almost charges at Annie.
options.D: Jack wakes up by a stream, sees a tiger drinking the water, and hides in the mud until the tiger finally leaves.

evidence: “Thanks for the ride,” he said softly.
The rhino rose from the stream. He looked like an ancient swamp creature.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：Jack wakes up by a misty stream, slides off Saba into the mud, and reads about rhinos just before one rises from the water and almost charges at Annie.

questions.stem: What was wrong with the tiger that Annie found?

options.A: He had fallen into a deep muddy hole.
options.B: He had been squeezed by the python.
options.C: His front paw was caught in a trap.
options.D: He was stuck high up in a tree.

evidence: The tiger was lying on his side, completely still.
His front paw was caught in a trap.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：His front paw was caught in a trap.

questions.stem: The book says that if the killing does not end, tigers and rhinos “face extinction.” “Extinction” means ___.

options.A: 被关进动物园
options.B: 搬到别的森林去生活
options.C: 生病或受伤
options.D: 灭绝（世界上再也没有这种动物）

evidence: Extinction means that someday there may be no Indian tigers or rhinos left on earth.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“灭绝（世界上再也没有这种动物）”。

questions.stem: Annie says the trapped tiger “must have gotten caught last night. That’s the sad sound we heard.” Which earlier sound is she talking about?

options.A: The screeching and cawing of the birds when they first landed.
options.B: The long roar that turned into moaning while they rode the elephants.
options.C: The short barking sounds the small deer made in the forest.
options.D: The slurpy, sloshing sound the rhino made in the stream.

evidence: He must have gotten caught last night. That’s the sad sound we heard.
questions.rationale: 结合人物与事件的关系，正确的是：The long roar that turned into moaning while they rode the elephants.

questions.stem: After reading the book, what makes Jack say, “Oh, man, we do have to save him”?

options.A: He learns that poachers trap and kill tigers, and that tigers could become extinct.
options.B: He learns that tigers are gentle animals that never attack people.
options.C: He learns that the trap will soon snap shut on Annie’s hand.
options.D: He learns that the tiger is a pet that belongs to the hermit.

evidence: After trapping a tiger, they kill it and sell the body parts for money.
If the killing does not end, they both face extinction.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：He learns that poachers trap and kill tigers, and that tigers could become extinct.

questions.stem: Which event happens LAST in this chapter?

options.A: Jack pushes down the lever and raises the bar.
options.B: Annie strokes the tiger’s fur gently.
options.C: Jack shows Annie the picture of the trap.
options.D: The tiger gets to his feet and snarls at Jack and Annie.

evidence: The tiger was on his feet. He stared right at them.
The tiger snarled at Jack and Annie.
questions.rationale: 按照本章事件先后顺序，最先/最后发生的是：The tiger gets to his feet and snarls at Jack and Annie.

questions.stem: When Teddy barks fiercely at Annie, what does she say he is telling them?

options.A: To climb a tree.
options.B: To run and hide.
options.C: To stand still and be quiet.
options.D: To fight the tiger together.

evidence: “Teddy says run and hide!” said Annie.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：To run and hide.

questions.stem: After the tiger leaves, “Teddy was just like a small scruffy dog again.” “Scruffy” means ___.

options.A: 凶猛可怕的
options.B: 高大强壮的
options.C: 毛发蓬乱、脏兮兮的
options.D: 干净整洁的

evidence: Teddy was just like a small scruffy dog again.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“毛发蓬乱、脏兮兮的”。

questions.stem: Jack hears growls grow “louder and louder” and says, “That doesn’t sound like Teddy.” Later he asks Teddy, “Did you turn into a wild dog?” What do these clues suggest?

options.A: Teddy may have used some kind of magic to become fierce enough to scare off the tiger.
options.B: A real pack of wild dogs came out of the forest to help Jack and Annie.
options.C: The tiger was growling at the langurs in the trees, not at Teddy.
options.D: Teddy ran away and hid behind the big black rock with Jack and Annie.

evidence: “That doesn’t sound like Teddy,” said Jack.
Did you turn into a wild dog?
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：Teddy may have used some kind of magic to become fierce enough to scare off the tiger.

questions.stem: Why does Jack say, “I guess we won’t be getting a thank-you gift from that tiger”?

options.A: Tigers have no way to carry presents through the forest.
options.B: Teddy had already gotten the gift from the tiger.
options.C: The langurs told Jack the gift was hidden somewhere else.
options.D: The tiger they had just saved came after them instead of thanking them.

evidence: The huge tiger limped closer and closer to Jack and Annie.
“Well, I guess we won’t be getting a thank-you gift from that tiger,” he said.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：The tiger they had just saved came after them instead of thanking them.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes this chapter?

options.A: The freed tiger comes after Jack and Annie, Teddy bravely drives him away, and the langurs lead the children downstream to a peaceful old man.
options.B: The freed tiger becomes friends with Jack and Annie, licks their hands, and then gives them a thank-you gift from the forest.
options.C: Jack and Annie run from the tiger all the way back to the tree house, and then they wish themselves home to Frog Creek.
options.D: Teddy chases the rhino out of the stream, the elephants come back for the children, and Saba carries them to the tree house.

evidence: Teddy stood tall and brave in the grass.
When they went around the bend, they saw a man sitting cross-legged on a rock.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：The freed tiger comes after Jack and Annie, Teddy bravely drives him away, and the langurs lead the children downstream to a peaceful old man.

questions.stem: The blind man says, “Hermits live far away from other people.” A “hermit” is ___.

options.A: 看守森林的人
options.B: 偷猎者
options.C: 驯兽师
options.D: 隐士（独自远离人群生活的人）

evidence: “Hermits live far away from other people,” said the blind man.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“隐士（独自远离人群生活的人）”。

questions.stem: How does the hermit say he learns from nature?

options.A: He listens to the sounds of the forest animals.
options.B: He reads many books about the forest animals.
options.C: He walks through the forest every single night.
options.D: He asks the langurs to teach him their language.

evidence: “I listen,” said the blind man.
To the chatter of the monkeys, the rumble of the elephant, the roar of the tiger,” said the man.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：He listens to the sounds of the forest animals.

questions.stem: The hermit says the lotus blossom’s “beauty cannot live without its ugliness.” What is he teaching Jack and Annie about the tiger?

options.A: The tiger is too ugly and dangerous, so he should not have been saved.
options.B: A lotus flower can keep people safe from the wild tigers of the forest.
options.C: Saving the tiger means accepting both his beauty and his fierce, wild nature.
options.D: Beautiful things should always be kept far away from dark, thick mud.

evidence: This perfect lotus blossom grows from dark, thick mud,” he said. “Its beauty cannot live without its ugliness.
“When you saved the tiger, you saved all of him,” said the blind man.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：Saving the tiger means accepting both his beauty and his fierce, wild nature.

questions.stem: Why is the tree house close by, even though Jack thought they had traveled far away?

options.A: The tree house magically followed them through the forest all night.
options.B: The elephants walked in a large circle, so they are back where they started.
options.C: The hermit carried the tree house to a tree beside his cave.
options.D: The langurs led them back by a shortcut across the stream.

evidence: The elephants walked in a large circle. So you are back at the place where you started.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：The elephants walked in a large circle, so they are back where they started.

questions.stem: How is the lotus blossom connected to Morgan’s note?

options.A: It is the “gift from a kangaroo,” which the hermit brought from a faraway land.
options.B: It is the “gift from a ship lost at sea,” which washed up in the stream.
options.C: It is the “gift from a forest far away,” given to thank them for saving the tiger.
options.D: It is a present for Morgan’s garden, which the langurs picked just for her.

evidence: Take this lotus as a thank-you gift from all the forest for saving our fierce friend,
“A gift from a forest far away,” she said.
questions.rationale: 结合人物与事件的关系，正确的是：It is the “gift from a forest far away,” given to thank them for saving the tiger.

questions.stem: How does Annie say she knew that Teddy wanted them to hide behind the rock?

options.A: Teddy pointed at the big rock with his paw.
options.B: She just knew—she thinks she saw it in his eyes.
options.C: The hermit told her about it afterward.
options.D: She read about it in the India book.

evidence: “I just knew,” she said. “I think I saw it in his eyes.”
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：She just knew—she thinks she saw it in his eyes.

questions.stem: “The Frog Creek woods were very tame after the forest in India.” Here “tame” means ___.

options.A: 危险的；野性的
options.B: 茂密的；昏暗的
options.C: 吵闹的；喧哗的
options.D: 平静的；不危险的

evidence: The Frog Creek woods were very tame after the forest in India.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“平静的；不危险的”。

questions.stem: Teddy’s eyes “twinkled, as if they held many secrets,” and Jack whispers, “Who are you, really?” This suggests that Jack ___.

options.A: thinks that Teddy is sick and needs to see a doctor
options.B: has suddenly forgotten the little dog’s name
options.C: suspects that Teddy is much more than an ordinary little dog
options.D: believes that Teddy really belongs to the hermit

evidence: Teddy’s eyes twinkled, as if they held many secrets.
“Who are you, really?” whispered Jack.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：suspects that Teddy is much more than an ordinary little dog

questions.stem: Why does Annie tell Teddy, “One more gift, and you’ll be free from your spell”?

options.A: They now have three of the four special gifts that Morgan’s note asked for.
options.B: Morgan told them that only one more trip to India was needed.
options.C: The hermit promised to send them the very last gift himself.
options.D: Teddy already broke most of the spell by fighting the tiger.

evidence: “One more gift,” she said to Teddy, “and you’ll be free from your spell.”
questions.rationale: 结合人物与事件的关系，正确的是：They now have three of the four special gifts that Morgan’s note asked for.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes the whole book?

options.A: Jack and Annie travel to the Great Plains, live with the Lakota Indians, hunt buffalo on the open prairie, and receive an eagle’s feather as the second gift to help free Teddy.
options.B: Jack and Annie travel to a forest in India, escape a python and a tiger with help from langurs and elephants, free a trapped tiger, and receive a lotus as the third gift to help free Teddy.
options.C: Jack and Annie travel on the Titanic, help two children escape the sinking ship, ride in a lifeboat all night, and bring home a pocket watch as the first gift to help free Teddy.
options.D: Jack and Annie travel to Australia, rescue a baby kangaroo from a raging fire, and bring home a gift from the kangaroo as the fourth and final gift to free Teddy.

evidence: “Our third gift,” said Annie.
She put the lotus blossom beside the pocket watch from the Titanic and the eagle’s feather from the Lakota Indians.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：Jack and Annie travel to a forest in India, escape a python and a tiger with help from langurs and elephants, free a trapped tiger, and receive a lotus as the third gift to help free Teddy.

questions.stem: Which gifts from Jack and Annie’s first three trips are sitting beside Morgan’s note?

options.A: A seashell from the ocean, a buffalo horn from the prairie, and a tiger’s tooth from India.
options.B: A gold coin from a sunken ship, an eagle’s egg from the mountains, and a mango from India.
options.C: A pocket watch from the Titanic, a piece of painted bark, and a kangaroo’s tooth.
options.D: A pocket watch from the Titanic, an eagle’s feather from the prairie skies, and a lotus flower from India.

evidence: Two, an eagle’s feather from the prairie skies.
Three, a lotus flower from a forest in India.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：A pocket watch from the Titanic, an eagle’s feather from the prairie skies, and a lotus flower from India.

questions.stem: Jack “knew the note by heart now.” To know something “by heart” means to ___.

options.A: 打心底里喜欢
options.B: 能完整地背出来；牢牢记住
options.C: 心里感到害怕
options.D: 刚刚第一次读到

evidence: He knew the note by heart now:
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“能完整地背出来；牢牢记住”。

questions.stem: Why does Jack say, “We must be going to Australia”?

options.A: They still need a gift from a kangaroo, and Australia is where kangaroos live.
options.B: Morgan’s note says that the last gift is hidden somewhere in Australia.
options.C: Annie heard a kangaroo calling to them from the Frog Creek woods.
options.D: The lotus flower they brought home from India first came from Australia.

evidence: We just need to get a gift from a kangaroo,
“We must be going to Australia,” said Jack. “That’s where kangaroos live.”
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：They still need a gift from a kangaroo, and Australia is where kangaroos live.

questions.stem: After Teddy scratches at a book, Jack picks it up and says, “What’d I tell you?” before showing Annie the cover. Why does he say this?

options.A: He is upset that Teddy scratched and damaged the cover of the book.
options.B: He had told Annie that their next trip would take them back to India.
options.C: He had told Annie that Teddy knew how to read the titles of books.
options.D: The title, Adventure in Australia, proves that his guess about the trip was right.

evidence: “What’d I tell you?” he said. He showed the cover to Annie.
The title was Adventure in Australia.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：The title, Adventure in Australia, proves that his guess about the trip was right.

questions.stem: Which event happens FIRST in this chapter?

options.A: Jack and Annie hug Teddy inside the tree house.
options.B: Teddy scratches at a book lying in the corner.
options.C: Annie hears Teddy barking from the Frog Creek woods.
options.D: Jack points at a picture of a forest and makes a wish.

evidence: “Teddy’s calling us,” said Annie.
A faint bark came from the distance: Arf! Arf!
questions.rationale: 按照本章事件先后顺序，最先/最后发生的是：Annie hears Teddy barking from the Frog Creek woods.

questions.stem: According to Jack’s book, what does the name “koala” mean?

options.A: No drink.
options.B: Big foot.
options.C: Sleepy bear.
options.D: Gum-tree eater.

evidence: The name koala means “no drink,” because koalas rarely drink water.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：No drink.

questions.stem: “The emus gave the little dog a haughty look. Then they turned and walked proudly away.” Here “haughty” means ___.

options.A: 害怕的；胆小的
options.B: 友好的；亲切的
options.C: 傲慢的；高傲的
options.D: 饥饿的；贪吃的

evidence: The emus gave the little dog a haughty look. Then they turned and walked proudly away.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“傲慢的；高傲的”。

questions.stem: According to Jack’s book, why are wildfires a threat to koalas?

options.A: Koalas are afraid of loud noises and run straight into the fire.
options.B: Koalas are slow-moving and can’t escape the smoke and flames.
options.C: Koalas drink only from streams, and the streams dry up in a fire.
options.D: Koalas sleep in caves, and the smoke quickly fills up the caves.

evidence: Wildfires are also a threat. Koalas are slow-moving and can’t escape the smoke and flames.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：Koalas are slow-moving and can’t escape the smoke and flames.

questions.stem: Annie asks the sleeping koala, “Don’t you feel well?” Why does Jack tell her not to worry?

options.A: His book says koalas are not really bears, so they can never get sick.
options.B: He can tell that the koala is only pretending to be asleep.
options.C: He knows that someone who takes care of koalas lives nearby.
options.D: His book says koalas sleep during the hot day, so the koala is just sleepy, not sick.

evidence: “Don’t worry,” said Jack. “Listen to this.”
Koalas, like kangaroos, are active at night and sleep during the day when the sun is hot.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：His book says koalas sleep during the hot day, so the koala is just sleepy, not sick.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes this chapter?

options.A: Jack and Annie land in a dry Australian forest, smell smoke they think comes from campers, and meet emus and a sleepy koala while they look for water.
options.B: Jack and Annie land in a rainy forest, swim in a cool stream, and meet a mother kangaroo and her baby in the tall grass.
options.C: Jack and Annie land beside a busy campsite, eat dinner with the campers, and watch the emus race each other.
options.D: Jack and Annie land in a burning forest, run into a dark cave, and hide from the flames with a koala.

evidence: The tree house had landed in a scrubby forest filled with droopy plants and dry brown trees.
“Maybe people are camping over there,” Jack said.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：Jack and Annie land in a dry Australian forest, smell smoke they think comes from campers, and meet emus and a sleepy koala while they look for water.

questions.stem: According to Jack’s book, what does “macropod,” the scientists’ name for the kangaroo, mean?

options.A: No drink.
options.B: Laughing donkey.
options.C: Big foot.
options.D: Baby in a pouch.

evidence: Scientists call the kangaroo a macropod, which means “big foot.”
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：Big foot.

questions.stem: “Jack couldn’t believe how graceful the kangaroo was. She seemed to fly through the air, then land as softly as a butterfly.” “Graceful” means ___.

options.A: 笨重的；动作缓慢的
options.B: 凶猛的；样子吓人的
options.C: 感激的；心怀感谢的
options.D: 优美的；动作轻盈优雅的

evidence: Jack couldn’t believe how graceful the kangaroo was.
She seemed to fly through the air, then land as softly as a butterfly.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“优美的；动作轻盈优雅的”。

questions.stem: According to Jack’s book, why is the kookaburra also called the “laughing donkey”?

options.A: The strange sound it makes reminds people of a braying donkey.
options.B: It has a long face and big ears just like a donkey.
options.C: It likes to ride on the backs of donkeys and laugh.
options.D: It carries heavy loads of sticks back to its nest.

evidence: This is because the strange sound it makes reminds people of a braying donkey.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：The strange sound it makes reminds people of a braying donkey.

questions.stem: The kangaroo starts stamping her feet, then she freezes, and Teddy growls from Jack’s backpack. What do these clues suggest?

options.A: The kangaroo wants Annie to start another hopping contest.
options.B: Teddy is hungry and wants to eat the kangaroo’s grass.
options.C: They sense danger nearby—wild dogs are creeping toward the clearing.
options.D: A big thunderstorm is about to roll into the dry forest.

evidence: Grrr. Teddy growled from Jack’s backpack.
A moment later, three dogs crept silently into the clearing.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：They sense danger nearby—wild dogs are creeping toward the clearing.

questions.stem: Which event happens LAST in this chapter?

options.A: Annie and the kangaroo hop around each other.
options.B: The wild dogs race after the kangaroo and her baby.
options.C: Jack reads about the laughing kookaburra.
options.D: The kangaroo wakes up and glares at Jack and Annie.

evidence: Howling, the wild dogs raced after the kangaroo and her baby.
questions.rationale: 按照本章事件先后顺序，最先/最后发生的是：The wild dogs race after the kangaroo and her baby.

questions.stem: According to Jack’s book, what is the biggest enemy of the kangaroo?

options.A: The emu, the large bird that doesn’t fly.
options.B: The dingo, the wild dog of Australia.
options.C: The kookaburra, the laughing bird.
options.D: The koala, which lives in gum trees.

evidence: The biggest enemy of the kangaroo is the dingo, the wild dog of Australia.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：The dingo, the wild dog of Australia.

questions.stem: When Jack sees the big black cloud of smoke, “A feeling of dread came over Jack.” “Dread” means ___.

options.A: 恐惧；担心坏事就要发生
options.B: 兴奋；非常期待
options.C: 困倦；很想睡觉
options.D: 饥饿；很想吃东西

evidence: A feeling of dread came over Jack.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“恐惧；担心坏事就要发生”。

questions.stem: According to Jack’s book, why might a mother kangaroo throw her joey out of her pouch when dingoes chase her?

options.A: She is angry that Jack and Annie woke her up, so she no longer wants to carry him.
options.B: Her joey has grown too big and too heavy to ride in her pouch ever again.
options.C: She wants Jack and Annie to keep her baby and take him back home with them.
options.D: Without the extra weight, she can leap faster and farther and lead the dingoes away from her baby.

evidence: Without the extra weight in her pouch, she can leap faster and farther.
She then leads the dingoes away from her baby.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：Without the extra weight, she can leap faster and farther and lead the dingoes away from her baby.

questions.stem: When Annie says Jack looks “just like a mother kangaroo,” Jack says, “Oh, brother.” But then he pats the baby’s soft fur. This shows that Jack ___.

options.A: is angry at Annie and wants to give Joey back
options.B: feels a little silly but still cares about Joey
options.C: is afraid that Joey will bite his fingers
options.D: does not like animals with soft fur

evidence: “There,” Annie said. “You look just like a mother kangaroo.”
“Oh, brother,” said Jack. But he patted the baby’s soft fur.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：feels a little silly but still cares about Joey

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes this chapter?

options.A: Jack and Annie chase the dingoes away, bring the joey back to his mother, and receive a special gift from her.
options.B: Jack and Annie find the campers cooking dinner, share their water, and fall asleep beside the warm bonfire.
options.C: Jack and Annie find the baby kangaroo his mother left behind, carry him in Jack’s pack, and then realize the smoke is coming from a wildfire.
options.D: Jack and Annie lose the joey in the tall grass, look for him all afternoon, and then hurry back to the tree house.

evidence: Beside her in the grass was the baby kangaroo.
“We’re looking at a wildfire!” he said.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：Jack and Annie find the baby kangaroo his mother left behind, carry him in Jack’s pack, and then realize the smoke is coming from a wildfire.

questions.stem: As the fire spreads, which animals fly or race past Jack and Annie?

options.A: The koala and the dingoes.
options.B: The mother kangaroo and her joey.
options.C: The kookaburra and the emus.
options.D: A flock of blackbirds and the emus.

evidence: Just then the kookaburra flew through the sky, cackling. The emus raced by at top speed.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：The kookaburra and the emus.

questions.stem: “Branches cracked and fell from the trees. Smoke billowed everywhere.” Here “billowed” means ___.

options.A: 慢慢地消散不见
options.B: （烟雾）大团大团地翻滚涌出
options.C: 被大雨浇灭了
options.D: 静静地飘落到地上

evidence: Branches cracked and fell from the trees. Smoke billowed everywhere.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“（烟雾）大团大团地翻滚涌出”。

questions.stem: Annie says, “I have to get something!” and runs off. Later she comes back through the smoke carrying the koala. How does this connect to what Jack read about koalas earlier?

options.A: Koalas can lead people out of the smoke, so Annie went to find a guide.
options.B: Koalas are the gift Morgan asked for, so Annie wanted to bring one home.
options.C: Koalas know where the tree house is, so Annie asked the koala for help.
options.D: Koalas are slow-moving and can’t escape fires, so Annie went back to save the koala.

evidence: “I’ll catch up!” said Annie. “I have to get something!”
She was carrying the koala.
questions.rationale: 结合人物与事件的关系，正确的是：Koalas are slow-moving and can’t escape fires, so Annie went back to save the koala.

questions.stem: Smoke hides the treetops, and Jack stumbles blindly through the brush. How does he find his way?

options.A: He follows the sound of Teddy’s barking.
options.B: He follows a map in the Australia book.
options.C: He follows the running emus to safety.
options.D: He follows the sound of Annie’s singing.

evidence: All he could do was follow the sound of Teddy’s barking.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：He follows the sound of Teddy’s barking.

questions.stem: Which event happens LAST in this chapter?

options.A: Annie dashes off in the other direction.
options.B: Teddy barks and vanishes inside a cave.
options.C: The emus race by at top speed.
options.D: Annie appears through the smoke carrying the koala.

evidence: Teddy barked again and vanished inside the cave.
questions.rationale: 按照本章事件先后顺序，最先/最后发生的是：Teddy barks and vanishes inside a cave.

questions.stem: When Teddy howls in the dark cave, what begins to glow?

options.A: A pair of yellow eyes belonging to a dingo hiding in the dark.
options.B: A painting of a mother kangaroo carrying her joey in her pouch.
options.C: A small fire that the campers left burning on the cave floor.
options.D: A white line that grows into a giant snake, with handprints below it.

evidence: The glowing line grew until it looked like a giant snake.
Then glowing handprints appeared below the snake.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：A white line that grows into a giant snake, with handprints below it.

questions.stem: “Suddenly Jack felt something thump against his leg. He stopped and gasped.” To “gasp” means to ___.

options.A: 哈哈大笑
options.B: 打一个大哈欠
options.C: （因吃惊或害怕）倒抽一口气
options.D: 轻轻地哼歌

evidence: Suddenly Jack felt something thump against his leg. He stopped and gasped.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“（因吃惊或害怕）倒抽一口气”。

questions.stem: Why do Jack and Annie hold hands as they walk into the cave?

options.A: It is too dark to see, so they stay together and follow Teddy’s bark.
options.B: They are dancing the same way Annie danced with the kangaroo.
options.C: Morgan’s note told them to hold hands inside every cave.
options.D: The cave floor is slippery with water from the rain.

evidence: “I can’t see anything,” said Jack.
“I guess we’ll have to follow Teddy’s bark,” said Annie. “Let’s hold hands.”
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：It is too dark to see, so they stay together and follow Teddy’s bark.

questions.stem: Right after Jack and Annie put their hands inside the painted handprints, they hear a loud boom, and soon they step out into a pouring rain. What does this hint?

options.A: The booming sound came from the walls of the cave falling down behind them.
options.B: The fire had reached the cave and was cracking the rocks into pieces.
options.C: Teddy was making the booming noise to scare the dingoes away.
options.D: Touching the painting seemed to bring a storm, as if the painting had some kind of magic.

evidence: She let go of Jack and put her hand inside one of the painted handprints.
“It sounded like thunder,” said Annie.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：Touching the painting seemed to bring a storm, as if the painting had some kind of magic.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes this chapter?

options.A: Jack and Annie hide in a cave all night until the fire burns out, and then they find the tree house in the morning.
options.B: Jack and Annie hold hands and follow Teddy into a dark cave, put their hands on a glowing snake painting, and come out into a thunderstorm.
options.C: Jack and Annie find the mother kangaroo hiding deep in a cave and give her baby back to her.
options.D: Jack and Annie get lost in a dark cave after Teddy runs away, and they call for Morgan to help them.

evidence: Jack and Annie climbed onto the rock ledge and stepped into the cave.
Annie pulled Jack toward the mouth of the cave and out into a pouring rain.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：Jack and Annie hold hands and follow Teddy into a dark cave, put their hands on a glowing snake painting, and come out into a thunderstorm.

questions.stem: Where does Annie put the koala after the rain begins?

options.A: In the fork of two branches of an unburned gum tree.
options.B: Inside Jack’s backpack, right next to Joey.
options.C: On the rock ledge at the mouth of the cave.
options.D: Back inside the magic tree house.

evidence: They walked over to the unburned gum tree. Annie placed the koala in the fork of two branches.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：In the fork of two branches of an unburned gum tree.

questions.stem: When Jack looks back at the woods, “misty steam was rising from the charred ground and burning bushes.” Here “charred” means ___.

options.A: 长满青苔的
options.B: 烧焦的；烧黑的
options.C: 冻得硬邦邦的
options.D: 刚翻过土的

evidence: misty steam was rising from the charred ground and burning bushes.
The heavy rain was putting out the wildfire.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“烧焦的；烧黑的”。

questions.stem: Annie says the storm “wasn’t just luck. It was magic,” but Jack answers, “That doesn’t make sense.” What does this show about Jack and Annie?

options.A: Jack believes in magic much more than Annie does.
options.B: Both of them think the storm came only by luck.
options.C: Annie believes the glowing painting brought the storm, while Jack looks for a sensible explanation.
options.D: Annie thinks the koala brought the storm, and Jack agrees with her.

evidence: “Yeah, the glowing hands and the snake,” said Annie. “Somehow they brought the storm.”
“That doesn’t make sense,” said Jack.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：Annie believes the glowing painting brought the storm, while Jack looks for a sensible explanation.

questions.stem: Teddy leads Jack and Annie to the Australia book lying on the wet ground. Why does finding the book tell them they are in the right spot?

options.A: Jack had left the book on the ground in the spot where they found Joey.
options.B: Morgan had placed the book there to mark the way to the tree house.
options.C: The mother kangaroo had carried the book there in her pouch.
options.D: The wind from the storm had blown the book out of the cave.

evidence: He stood over the Australia book. It was wet but not burned.
I left our book in the spot where we found Joey.
questions.rationale: 结合人物与事件的关系，正确的是：Jack had left the book on the ground in the spot where they found Joey.

questions.stem: Which event happens LAST in this chapter?

options.A: Annie places the koala in an unburned gum tree.
options.B: Teddy finds the wet Australia book.
options.C: The heavy rain turns into a drizzle.
options.D: They hear the squishy sound of big feet slapping through mud.

evidence: It was the sound of big feet slapping through mud.
questions.rationale: 按照本章事件先后顺序，最先/最后发生的是：They hear the squishy sound of big feet slapping through mud.

questions.stem: What gift does the mother kangaroo give Jack and Annie?

options.A: A soft tuft of brown fur from her baby joey.
options.B: A small piece of bark with a tiny painting of the snake on it.
options.C: A smooth stone from the floor of the painted cave.
options.D: A gum leaf she picked from the koala’s tree.

evidence: Then she bent over and used a front paw to pick up a small piece of bark from the wet grass.
There was a tiny painting on it. It was just like the snake painting in the cave.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：A small piece of bark with a tiny painting of the snake on it.

questions.stem: Jack’s book says, “In special ceremonies, they sometimes honor the Rainbow Serpent by painting their handprints on the magic snake.” A “ceremony” is ___.

options.A: 比赛；竞赛
options.B: 课堂；学校
options.C: 集市；市场
options.D: 仪式；典礼

evidence: In special ceremonies, they sometimes honor the Rainbow Serpent by painting their handprints on the magic snake.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“仪式；典礼”。

questions.stem: After hearing what Jack reads, why does Annie think the Rainbow Serpent sent the rain?

options.A: The mother kangaroo showed Annie that the Rainbow Serpent lives up in the rain clouds.
options.B: Jack’s book says that the Rainbow Serpent puts out every wildfire in Australia.
options.C: In Dreamtime the Rainbow Serpent sends life-giving rain, and putting their hands on its painting was like a special ceremony.
options.D: Teddy barked at the sky to tell Annie that the snake was on its way.

evidence: In Dreamtime, there is a Rainbow Serpent who sends life-giving rain.
It was like a special ceremony.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：In Dreamtime the Rainbow Serpent sends life-giving rain, and putting their hands on its painting was like a special ceremony.

questions.stem: Jack says the Rainbow Serpent is “in Dreamtime, not real time.” Then Annie points to a rainbow in the sky, and Jack shivers even though the air is warm. What does his shiver suggest?

options.A: He is cold because a chilly wind has started to blow through the forest.
options.B: He is beginning to feel that something mysterious and magical really happened.
options.C: He is afraid the mother kangaroo will come back and stamp at them.
options.D: He is getting sick from breathing in smoke from the wildfire.

evidence: A rainbow curved across the blue Australian sky.
Though the air was warm again, he shivered.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：He is beginning to feel that something mysterious and magical really happened.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes this chapter?

options.A: Joey’s mother returns, gives Jack and Annie a bark painting of the Rainbow Serpent as a thank-you, and the children head home with all four gifts.
options.B: Joey’s mother never returns, so Jack and Annie decide to take Joey home with them to Frog Creek.
options.C: The dingoes come back and chase the mother kangaroo away, and Teddy fights them off in the rain.
options.D: Jack and Annie paint their own handprints on a piece of bark and give it to the mother kangaroo as a gift.

evidence: The mother kangaroo bounded out of the trees.
“Hey, we have all four gifts now,” said Annie.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：Joey’s mother returns, gives Jack and Annie a bark painting of the Rainbow Serpent as a thank-you, and the children head home with all four gifts.

questions.stem: According to Morgan, what does the eagle’s feather teach the boy?

options.A: That time is very precious and must be used wisely.
options.B: That nature holds many wonders.
options.C: That a small creature can be one of the bravest.
options.D: That there is wisdom in the traditions of ancient peoples.

evidence: The eagle’s feather teaches him that a small creature can be one of the bravest.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：That a small creature can be one of the bravest.

questions.stem: Morgan says the watch “teaches him that time is very precious. It must be used wisely.” Here “precious” means ___.

options.A: 宝贵的；珍贵的
options.B: 无聊的；没意思的
options.C: 飞快的；匆忙的
options.D: 免费的；不要钱的

evidence: This watch teaches him that time is very precious. It must be used wisely.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“宝贵的；珍贵的”。

questions.stem: Morgan says, “Sometimes the boy didn’t want to study other times and places.” Which gift teaches him the lesson he needed for this?

options.A: The lotus flower from the forest in India.
options.B: The pocket watch from the Titanic.
options.C: The eagle’s feather from the Lakota Indians.
options.D: The bark painting of the Rainbow Serpent.

evidence: Sometimes the boy didn’t want to study other times and places,
This painting teaches him there is mystery, magic, and wisdom in the traditions of ancient peoples.
questions.rationale: 结合人物与事件的关系，正确的是：The bark painting of the Rainbow Serpent.

questions.stem: Morgan keeps talking about “the boy,” and Jack asks, “What boy?” Based on the end of the chapter, who was the boy Morgan meant?

options.A: Jack, because he sometimes wastes time and feels afraid.
options.B: A boy from Camelot whom Jack and Annie have never met.
options.C: Teddy—the little dog under the spell was really a boy.
options.D: One of the children Jack and Annie met on the Titanic.

evidence: He was no longer a dog.
He was a boy.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：Teddy—the little dog under the spell was really a boy.

questions.stem: Which event happens FIRST in this chapter?

options.A: Morgan explains what the lotus flower teaches.
options.B: Annie shows Morgan the piece of painted bark.
options.C: Jack asks Morgan, “What boy?”
options.D: Teddy changes from a dog into a boy.

evidence: She reached into Jack’s pack and pulled out the piece of painted bark.
questions.rationale: 按照本章事件先后顺序，最先/最后发生的是：Annie shows Morgan the piece of painted bark.

questions.stem: According to Morgan, what is Ted training to do?

options.A: To become a brave knight of Camelot.
options.B: To be a sailor on great ships at sea.
options.C: To teach school in the town of Frog Creek.
options.D: To work in Morgan’s library at Camelot.

evidence: “Ted is training to work in my library at Camelot,” said Morgan.
questions.rationale: 原文直接写到：To work in Morgan’s library at Camelot.

questions.stem: After Morgan tells him to ask before trying her spells, “The boy grinned sheepishly.” “Sheepishly” means ___.

options.A: 不好意思地；有点难为情地
options.B: 得意洋洋地
options.C: 气呼呼地
options.D: 吓得发抖地

evidence: The boy grinned sheepishly.
questions.rationale: 结合原句语境，这个词在这里最接近“不好意思地；有点难为情地”。

questions.stem: Why does Morgan tell the boy, “I hope next time you’ll ask before trying the spells in my spell book”?

options.A: He had lost her spell book somewhere on the Titanic.
options.B: He had tried her spells without asking and accidentally changed himself into a dog.
options.C: He had used a spell to make the tree house spin too fast.
options.D: He had turned Jack and Annie into kangaroos by mistake.

evidence: And I hope next time you’ll ask before trying the spells in my spell book,
“I accidentally changed myself into a dog,” he said.
questions.rationale: 结合事件的原因、目的或结果，正确关系是：He had tried her spells without asking and accidentally changed himself into a dog.

questions.stem: At the end, Annie says their adventures with Teddy were “Like living in Dreamtime,” and Jack agrees. What does she mean?

options.A: They slept through all four adventures and only dreamed about them.
options.B: Their adventures were quiet and boring, like lying in bed at night.
options.C: They want to move to Australia and live there forever.
options.D: Their adventures felt magical and full of mystery, like the old stories of Dreamtime.

evidence: “Like living in Dreamtime,” said Annie.
That was exactly what it was like.
questions.rationale: 原文细节支持这一推断：Their adventures felt magical and full of mystery, like the old stories of Dreamtime.

questions.stem: Which choice best summarizes the whole book?

options.A: Jack and Annie travel to a forest in India, escape a python and a tiger, free a trapped tiger, and receive a lotus flower as the third gift to help free Teddy.
options.B: Jack and Annie travel to the Great Plains, live with the Lakota Indians, and receive an eagle’s feather as the second gift to help free Teddy.
options.C: Jack and Annie travel to Australia, care for a baby kangaroo and escape a wildfire, receive a bark painting of the Rainbow Serpent as the fourth gift, and break the spell so Teddy turns back into a boy.
options.D: Jack and Annie travel to Australia, catch a sleepy koala for Morgan’s library, and decide to keep Teddy as their own pet dog in Frog Creek.

evidence: You helped break the spell.
“Meet my young helper from Camelot,” said Morgan.
questions.rationale: 这个选项同时保留了本章开端与后续的关键事件：Jack and Annie travel to Australia, care for a baby kangaroo and escape a wildfire, receive a bark painting of the Rainbow Serpent as the fourth gift, and break the spell so Teddy turns back into a boy.
